newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga takes trip down memory lane when she pays visit to her old school in France, the Political Science Institute of the University of Aix Marseille. Kumaratunga is on official visit to that country.
Government waives import duty on all varieties of rice to curb rising local prices.
Government para-medics decide not to work on weekends if health authorities do not solve their grievances pertaining to salary and work conditions.

Tamil Tiger leader Velupillai Prabhakaran says government peddling a false peace plan to divert international pressure. Prabhakaran delivered address over the Tigers' clandestine radio to mark the rebels' Heroes Day on November 27.
Nominations called from December 11 to 18 for local government elections in the northern districts of Jaffna, Kilinochchi, Vavuniya and Mannar.
Ten trade unions urge main opposition United National Party to put forth alternative proposals to end country's 13-year ethnic war, if they cannot agree to the ones presented by the government.
Tamil Tigers send four women suicide bombers into Colombo to kill a leading government personality, police say.
Troops launch offensive against Tamil guerrillas near their forward defences at Nochchimodai north of Vavuniya town.
Nominations called from December 11 to 18 for local government elections in the northern districts of Jaffna, Kilinochchi, Vavuniya and Mannar.
